surface: Firstmate native Herdr state, recovery and task notifications; tmux fallback
isolation: Named fm-lab-* sessions through bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh; marked disposable FM_HOME; private Herdr configuration and harness roots; private tmux socket; guarded teardown and default-session tripwire
observations: Native working, idle, blocked and unknown states reached the public crew-state CLI.
Working, idle and unknown levels stayed quiet across complete watcher poll cycles; blocked episodes emitted one wake and notice until working re-armed them.
Killing a foreground process left a stale working registration, but recovery emitted once; closing its pane did not repeat recovery for that incarnation; a new incarnation re-armed it.
Confirmed missing endpoint remained actionable during a declared pause.
A live socket with mode 000 yielded unknown/unreadable and no watcher recovery after a complete cycle; its permissions were restored before teardown.
Trusted Claude lifecycle busy evidence kept native idle classified working, then an idle lifecycle event restored idle.
PR-ready notifications used a short task label; mixed PR/decision batches emitted one decision notice; ordinary blocked/failed and resolved decisions emitted none.
All four watcher-generated notification calls returned shown:true and had a durable wake already queued.
Real Claude, Codex and Pi CLIs reached settled states in isolated Herdr panes; this startup smoke did not execute model turns.
Tmux fallback classified a captain decision parked and delivered its status signal on a private server.
visual_limit: Captured the actual 120x40 Herdr viewer and rendered its terminal grid. Native desktop notices are outside that grid; no desktop screenshot API is available. Herdr returned shown:true for both titles.
